question.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
\displaystyle \iiint\limits_R 4x^3  \: \mathrm{d}V
$$

where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (y,z) \in D, \: 0 \leq x \leq \sqrt{y} \right\},
$$

and $D$ is a finite region in $yz$-plane enclosed between the $y$-axis, the $z$-axis, and the line $z = 4-y$ in the first quadrant.
question.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a mixed integral, we obtain

$$
\displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} 4x^3 \, \textrm{d}V
= 
\iint\limits_{D} \left[ \int_{0}^{\sqrt{y}} 4x^3 \, \mathrm{d}x \right] \mathrm{d}A.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{y}}4{x}^{3}\,dx]dA & ={∬}_{D}[{x}^{4}]_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{y}}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}{(\sqrt{y})}^{4}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

We must now evaluate this double integral over the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216491/assets/3c8712fa0a30ad94f503efe5e080ee89f83eb21f19fba45033bbedeab08ac816.png)

We can evaluate our double integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{4-y}{y}^{2}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}[{\int }_{0}^{4-y}{y}^{2}\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}[{y}^{2}z]_{z=0}^{z=4-y}dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{y}^{2}(4-y)\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}4{y}^{2}-{y}^{3}\,dy \\  & ={[\frac{4}{3}{y}^{3}-\frac{1}{4}{y}^{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=4} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}(64-0)-\frac{1}{4}(256-0) \\  & =\frac{64}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
